children: Hungary's central bank announced on Tuesday that it had reduced its medium-term inflation target to 2.5% from 3%, which will come into effect over the monetary policy horizon on Jan. 1, 2028 as the country prepares to meet the conditions of euro entry.

"The lower inflation, the decrease in domestic risk premia, and the continued stability of the foreign exchange market support anchoring expectations at a lower level. Together, these factors provide a suitable environment for lowering the inflation target to 2.5%," the bank's Monetary Council said after its rate-setting meeting.
